steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper DemoCaricature, about generating personalised caricatures from a portrait photo plus a rough sketch. Keep the playful, conversational tone, explain the identity-vs-abstraction challenge, why prior caricature and personalisation methods fall short, our two technical ideas, and the contributions.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- Hook: democratising caricature generation for everyone
- Core question: is this me? identity vs abstraction, and user individuality
- Our solution: a rough sketch
- Prior caricature work and its shortcomings
- Approach: T2I personalisation + sketch T2I-Adapter, and why it's hard
- Explicit Rank-1 Model Editing and Random Mask Reconstruction
- Contributions

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- Hook
  - personalised caricature, e.g. on holiday
  - democratise caricature generation for everyone
  - input: portrait + conceptual sketch -> high-fidelity caricature capturing your essence
  - not replacing artists; art may never be fully conquered by AI; get one done in Paris by an artist
- Core question
  - "Is this me?" (Obama, Mr. Bean in figure)
  - balance: abstraction for caricature look vs identity cues
  - inject individuality and creativity so the caricature is yours, not dictated by AI
- Sketch as solution
  - single rough sketch encapsulates your vision (figure)
  - challenge: regardless of artistic skill, plausible caricature + preserved identity
  - also accommodate a preferred caricature style
- Prior work
  - not pioneers; motivated by prior art
  - our challenges exceed previous systems, esp. deformation-based ones (style over identity)
  - prior systems leave "you" out
  - result: less expressive, missing local abstraction, hairstyle variation, view changes -> easy with one sketch in ours
- Approach
  - novel single-image T2I personalisation module (identity) + sketch-specific T2I-Adapter (sketch control)
  - single-image personalisation methods overfit -> specialised, inflexible, poor generalisation
  - hard to adapt to exaggerated, subjective, OOD human sketches
  - merging identity and style blindly -> blended features, skewed caricatures
- Methods
  - Explicit Rank-1 Model Editing for single-sketch personalisation: learn and fuse identity and style
  - explicit editing of identity and style in cross-attention layers, minimal extra parameters, keeps textual context
  - subjective, fine-grained control; mitigates overfitting
  - Random Mask Reconstruction: mask random patches, focus on identity/style over local variations; handles exaggerated sketches
- Contributions
  - (i) democratise caricature generation from photo + sketch
  - (ii) abstraction vs identity via Explicit Rank-1 Editing on cross-attention layers
  - (iii) robustness via Random Mask Reconstruction

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Have you ever wondered when you would finally get that personalised caricature made, maybe during a holiday? Then this paper is for you – we want to democratise caricature generation for everyone! You give us a portrait of yourself and a conceptual sketch of how you see your caricature, and we automatically generate a high-fidelity caricature that clearly captures your essence. We are not trying to replace artists though; the realm of art may be one that AI will never fully conquer – so next time you are in Paris, do get your caricature made by a skilled artist!

We start our study with the basic question that comes up when you look at a caricature – Is this me? (or Obama or Mr. Bean for that matter in the figure?) The core challenge in caricature generation is getting the delicate balance between adding abstraction to get that distinctive caricature look, and still keeping the essential identity cues that clearly represent the intended person. On top of that, how do we inject your individuality and creativity into the art generation process, so the resulting caricature is really your own and not one decided only by AI?

Our solution is your sketch! A single rough sketch is all that is needed to capture your vision for your caricature, as shown in the figure. The scientific challenge is clear: no matter how much artistic skill you have or don't have, how can we design a system that generates a plausible caricature and still preserves your identity? And also, if you prefer a specific caricature style, we would like to support that preference too.

- Prior work
  - not pioneers; motivated by prior art
  - deformation-based systems: style over identity; leave "you" out
  - missing local abstraction, hairstyle variation, view changes
- Approach: single-image T2I personalisation (identity) + sketch T2I-Adapter; overfitting, OOD sketches, blending identity and style
- Methods: Explicit Rank-1 Model Editing (cross-attention, minimal params); Random Mask Reconstruction (random patches, robustness)
- Contributions (i)-(iii)

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Have you ever wondered when you would finally get that personalised caricature made, maybe during a holiday? Then this paper is for you – we want to democratise caricature generation for everyone! You give us a portrait of yourself and a conceptual sketch of how you see your caricature, and we automatically generate a high-fidelity caricature that clearly captures your essence. We are not trying to replace artists though; the realm of art may be one that AI will never fully conquer – so next time you are in Paris, do get your caricature made by a skilled artist!

We start our study with the basic question that comes up when you look at a caricature – Is this me? (or Obama or Mr. Bean for that matter in the figure?) The core challenge in caricature generation is getting the delicate balance between adding abstraction to get that distinctive caricature look, and still keeping the essential identity cues that clearly represent the intended person. On top of that, how do we inject your individuality and creativity into the art generation process, so the resulting caricature is really your own and not one decided only by AI?

Our solution is your sketch! A single rough sketch is all that is needed to capture your vision for your caricature, as shown in the figure. The scientific challenge is clear: no matter how much artistic skill you have or don't have, how can we design a system that generates a plausible caricature and still preserves your identity? And also, if you prefer a specific caricature style, we would like to support that preference too.

We are certainly not the first to do caricature generation; our motivation mainly comes from prior art in this field. But our set of challenges goes well beyond the technical capabilities of previous systems, especially the ones that are mainly deformation-based, which tend to put style creation before identity. Importantly, these prior systems often don't include “you” in the solution. Because of this the generated caricatures are less expressive and miss interesting features like local abstraction, hairstyle variation, and view changes – all of which can be easily added in our system with just your single sketch!

To model the balance between identity and style, our approach relies on the interaction between a new single-image Text-to-Image (T2I) personalisation module and a sketch-specific T2I-Adapter. The first one ensures identity, and the second one allows sketch-controlled caricature generation. This is not trivial. The latest single-image T2I personalisation approaches often have problems with overfitting during single-image fine-tuning, which gives a very specialised but inflexible model that does not generalise beyond the training data. This makes it especially hard for them to adapt to the highly exaggerated and subjective human sketches, which are often Out-of-Distribution (OOD). The challenge gets worse because we have to merge the concepts of identity and style. If this is done blindly, features get blended, and the caricatures lack distinction or lean towards one aspect at the expense of the other.

So we propose Explicit Rank-1 Model Editing for single-sketch personalisation, which allows effective learning and fusion of identity and style. It has an explicit mechanism that independently handles the explicit editing of identity and style in the cross-attention layers, with minimal extra parameters, while keeping the textual contexts intact. This gives more subjective and fine-grained control over the desired concepts and reduces the overfitting that usually happens. We also introduce Random Mask Reconstruction to make the model more robust to distorted shapes. It masks random patches of the input image, which forces the model to focus on the important identity and style features rather than local variations. This lets the model handle exaggerated caricature sketches better while emphasising the essential learned features.

Our contributions are: (i) we democratise caricature generation, so that individuals can easily create personalised caricatures from a photo and a conceptual sketch. (ii) we handle the delicate balance between abstraction and identity with Explicit Rank-1 Editing, which gives nuanced control by selectively applying rank-1 edits to cross-attention layers. (iii) we make the system more robust with Random Mask Reconstruction, so it can handle distorted shapes effectively while emphasising essential identity and style.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Ever wondered when you would finally get that personalised caricature made, perhaps during a holiday? Look no further, this paper is for you – we strive to democratise caricature [1,2,3] generation for everyone! With a portrait of yourself and a conceptual sketch of how you envision your caricature, we automatically generate a high-fidelity caricature that unmistakably captures your essence [3]. Our aim, however, is not to replace artists; the realm of art may be one that AI never entirely conquers – so when you next find yourself in Paris, do get your caricature crafted by a skilled artist!

We begin our study by asking the fundamental question that arises when scrutinising a caricature – Is this me? (or Obama or Mr. Bean for that matter in the figure?) Indeed, the core challenge in caricature generation is navigating the delicate balance between infusing abstraction [4] to achieve that distinctive caricature appearance and preserving the essential identity cues that unmistakably represent the intended person [5]. Above all, how do we inject your individuality [6] and creativity [7] into the art generation process, so that the resulting caricature is genuinely your own rather than one dictated solely by AI?

Our solution lies in your sketch! A single rough sketch [8,9,10] is all it takes to encapsulate your vision for your caricature, as illustrated in the figure. The scientific challenge is clear: regardless of your artistic skill or lack of it, how can we design a system that adeptly generates a plausible caricature while preserving your identity [3]? And if there is a specific caricature style you prefer, we would like to accommodate that preference as well.

We are certainly not pioneers in caricature generation [1,3,2]; our motivation draws primarily from prior art in this field. However, our set of challenges notably surpasses the technical capabilities of previous systems [3,1], particularly the primarily deformation-based ones [11,12], which tend to prioritise style creation over identity. Crucially, these systems often fall short of including “you” in the solution, so the generated caricatures lack expressiveness and miss interesting features like local abstraction [4], hairstyle variation [13], and view changes – all of which can easily be injected into our system with just your single sketch!

Our approach to modelling the balance between identity and style relies on the interaction between a novel single-image Text-to-Image (T2I) personalisation module and a sketch-specific T2I-Adapter [14]: the former ensures identity, while the latter allows sketch-controlled caricature generation. This is not trivial. Recent single-image T2I personalisation approaches [15,16,17] often grapple with overfitting during single-image fine-tuning, resulting in a highly specialised yet inflexible model that does not generalise beyond its training data. This makes it especially challenging for them to adapt to highly exaggerated and subjective human sketches, which are often Out-of-Distribution (OOD). The challenge is further exacerbated because we must merge the concepts of identity and style; done blindly, this leads to a blending of features and to caricatures that lack distinction or skew towards one aspect at the expense of the other.

We therefore propose Explicit Rank-1 Model Editing for single-sketch personalisation, enabling effective learning and fusion of identity and style. Through an explicit mechanism, it independently manipulates the editing of identity and style in the cross-attention layers [14], with minimal extra parameters, while maintaining the integrity of textual contexts. This provides more subjective and fine-grained control over the desired concepts and mitigates the overfitting typically encountered. Furthermore, we introduce Random Mask Reconstruction to improve robustness to distorted shapes. By masking random patches of the input image, it compels the model to focus on crucial identity and style features rather than local variations, allowing it to better handle exaggerated caricature sketches while emphasising the essential learned features.

Our contributions are: (i) we democratise caricature generation, enabling individuals to easily create personalised caricatures from a photo and a conceptual sketch. (ii) we address the delicate balance between abstraction and identity via Explicit Rank-1 Editing, offering nuanced control by selectively applying rank-1 edits to cross-attention layers. (iii) we enhance robustness with Random Mask Reconstruction, enabling effective handling of distorted shapes while emphasising essential identity and style.
